# Unavoidable inside facets at arbitrarily small invariant buffers

This is an exact actual-body counterexample to inside-free selection at a
fixed proper marked point, even as the invariant buffer parameter tends
to zero. It strengthens the finite-parameter example in
`candidate 777caee80bc87e0e`.
The marked point is not asserted to be globally deepest, and these bodies
are not asserted to be joint bad minima. The depth ratios here tend to
1/2, not to the OC target 2/9.

## 1. Compatible bodies, original mass, and the small invariant parameter

Fix 0<eta<=1/4096. Set n=1,d=2, P={-2,-1,0,1,2}, and

    (r_-2,r_-1,r_0,r_1,r_2)
       =(1,1+4eta,1+4eta,1+3eta,1+2eta),
    K_z=[-r_z/2,r_z/2] times [-1,1].                     (1)

The successive width increments are 4eta,0,-eta,-eta. Their nonincrease
makes the piecewise-affine interpolation r(z) concave, so

    C_eta={-2<=z<=2, |x|<=r(z)/2, |y|<=1}

is an actual convex body with exactly the displayed integer fibers.
Throughout, capture measure is the original mixed measure

    mu(B)=sum_(z in P) area(B_z),  M=mu(C_eta)=10+26eta.

Every fiber has mass at most 2+8eta<M/2. Every proper closed-minor count
quota is strict: a singleton has mass<M/2, while a closed minor with at
least two sites is a consecutive integer chain, has both occupied
parities, and, when proper, has mass<M. No heavy fiber or missing integer
base is concealed in this construction.

The within-fiber covariance average is diagonal, with

    Sigma_yy=1/3,
    Sigma_xx=(sum_z r_z^3)/(12 sum_z r_z),
    c_eta=Sigma_xx/Sigma_yy=(sum_z r_z^3)/(4 sum_z r_z).

For all eta<=1/16 (a larger range used for the estimates),

    1/4 <= c_eta <= 25/64.                               (2)

Indeed c_eta is one quarter of a weighted mean of r_z^2, and
1<=r_z<=5/4 in that range.

Let delta=2048eta<=1/2, choose the actual interior mark
Y_eta=(0,0,delta), and use the constant normalized parameter L=1. Write

    f_eta=(E_K0(0,delta)/M)^(1/3),
    epsilon_eta=delta sqrt(3)/f_eta.                     (3)

Here E_K(y)=inf_c int_K [1+c.(X-y)]^(-3) dX, over denominators positive
on K, is the previously defined ordinary projective energy. Thus the
physical vertical buffer is exactly epsilon_eta f_eta sqrt(Sigma_yy)
=delta. These are genuine invariant buffers, not prescribed Euclidean
offsets in place of the invariant norm.

Also epsilon_eta tends to zero. The source rectangle contains the
rectangle centered at (0,delta), of horizontal width r_0 and vertical
halfheight 1-delta. Its area is at least1. Jensen on this centered
subrectangle gives E_K0(0,delta)>=1 for every admissible denominator.
As M<11, f_eta>=11^(-1/3), and consequently

    0<epsilon_eta<=2048eta sqrt(3) 11^(1/3) ->0.          (4)

## 2. The all-normal cap claim and a symmetric-core lower bound

For an upward continuous normal, scale its vertical component to1 and
reflect x so its horizontal component is t>=0. The actual minimally
buffered cap at Y_eta is

    H_(t,a)={y+t x+a z+g(t)>=0},
    g(t)=delta (sqrt(1+c_eta t^2)-1).                    (5)

The claim is that its unique minimum over every ambient cap orientation
is attained at t=0,a=-1/2, with original raw mass

    Q_eta=5+(23/2)eta.                                  (6)

Write F_0(t,a) for the unbuffered cap y+t x+a z>=0 and F(t,a) for (5).
Decompose the actual set into a centrally symmetric core and two
disjoint residuals. The core has the whole own fiber, common widths
1+3eta at bases -1,+1, and common widths1 at bases -2,+2. Every
nonvertical through-origin cap captures exactly

    C_0=(1+4eta)+2(1+3eta)+2=5+10eta

of this core. The residual R_1, at base -1, consists of

    (1+3eta)/2<=|x|<=(1+4eta)/2, |y|<=1,

and has area2eta. The residual R_2, at base+2, consists of

    1/2<=|x|<=1/2+eta, |y|<=1,

and has area4eta. If a<=0, R_1 has nonnegative constant margin -a and
therefore contributes at least eta by central symmetry. If a>=0,
R_2 contributes at least2eta. Hence, for all continuous orientations,

    F_0>=5+11eta=Q_eta-eta/2;
    F_0>=5+12eta>Q_eta if a>=0.                          (7)

The same argument applies to horizontal continuous normals. It uses
actual disjoint pieces of the original fibers, not an independent
allocation of overlapping endpoint credits.

## 3. All sufficiently vertical directions, by exact clipping

At t=0 put a=-b, b>=0. Direct clipping gives

    F_0(0,-b)=5+13eta-3eta b,  0<=b<=1/2;
                5+11eta+eta b,  1/2<=b<=1;
                5+12eta,       b>=1.                    (8)

Together with (7) for a>=0, this has the unique minimum Q_eta at b=1/2.
For b outside [1/4,3/4], its gap over Q_eta is at least eta/4.

Let T=1/16. The core contribution is independent of angle. The captured
vertical length clamp(1+s,0,2) is 1-Lipschitz in s. Consequently,

    |F_0(t,a)-F_0(0,a)|
       <=t int_(R_1 horizontal strips union R_2 horizontal strips) |x| dx
       =t(3eta/2+11eta^2/4)
       <=(107/64)eta t.                                 (9)

For t<=T this is at most107eta/1024<eta/4. Thus all b outside
[1/4,3/4] remain strictly above Q_eta. The case a>=0 is already strict
by (7), without this perturbation bound.

It remains to treat b in [1/4,3/4], 0<=t<=T. The three middle fibers
stay proper, since 3/4+(5/8)T<1. The left endpoint cannot be empty,
and the right endpoint cannot be full. Set s=2b-1 and

    I_r(s)=int_(-r/2)^(r/2) (s+t x)_+ dx,
    J(s)=I_(1+2eta)(s)-I_1(s)
        =int_(1/2<=|x|<=1/2+eta) (s+t x)_+ dx.

Exact clipping, with every saturation retained, gives

    F_0(t,-b)=5+13eta-3eta b+J(s),
    F_0(t,-b)-Q_eta=J(s)-(3eta/2)s.                     (10)

For completeness, the three middle fibers contribute
3+11eta+eta b; the left endpoint contributes 1+2b-I_1(s); and the
right contributes I_(1+2eta)(-s). Use
I_r(-s)=I_r(s)-r s to obtain (10).

The integration set defining J is symmetric and has length2eta, so
Jensen gives J(s)>=2eta(s)_+. Thus the gap in (10) is at least eta s/2
when s>=0, and at least -3eta s/2 when s<=0. Both are strictly positive
unless s=0. At s=0 and t>0,

    J(0)=t(eta/2+eta^2/2)>0.                            (11)

We conclude that EVERY t in (0,T] and every real a gives
F_0(t,a)>Q_eta, already before the positive buffer increment.

## 4. Every remaining upward angle, by a monotone actual strip gain

Adding g(t)>=0 cannot decrease any fiber capture. Its own-fiber increase
Delta_0(t), for t>0, has the exact representation

    Delta_0(t)=r_0 Pr{|X+Y/t|<=g(t)/t},                  (12)

where X and Y are independent uniform variables on [-r_0/2,r_0/2]
and [-1,1]. The factor is r_0, half the own rectangle's area.

The ratio g(t)/t is strictly increasing. For a fixed h>=0,
v -> Pr{|X+v|<=h} is even and nonincreasing in |v|, by interval overlap.
Conditioning on |Y|, increasing t therefore increases the probability
with a fixed threshold; the threshold in (12) also increases. It follows
that Delta_0 is nondecreasing on (0,infinity).

At T=1/16, the shifted own strip is wholly within the constant vertical
section-density range, because

    (r_0/2)T+g(T)
      <=5/128+25/65536<1.

Here sqrt(1+v)-1<=v/2, delta<=1/2, and (2) were used. Hence
Delta_0(T)=r_0 g(T)>=g(T). Since sqrt(1+c_eta T^2)+1<3, (2) also gives

    g(T)=delta c_eta T^2/(sqrt(1+c_eta T^2)+1)
          >delta/3072=2eta/3>eta/2.                    (13)

For every t>=T, (7), (12), and (13) prove
F(t,a)>=F_0(t,a)+Delta_0(t)>Q_eta, uniformly in the choice of a.
Section3 treated 0<t<=T. At t=0 the buffer increment is0, so (8)
proves uniqueness of the upward minimum stated in (6).

## 5. Downward, horizontal, and pure-base normals

For a downward normal, reflection in y produces the same expression
as (5) with the larger constant

    delta(sqrt(1+c_eta t^2)+1)=g(t)+2delta.

Such a cap contains its upward counterpart. That counterpart is already
strictly above Q_eta unless t=0,a=-1/2. At these exceptional parameters
the extra2delta adds strictly positive own-fiber mass, since 0<delta<=1/2.
Thus every downward cap is strict too.

For a horizontal normal, reflect x and normalize its continuous
component to1. Its buffer shift is delta sqrt(c_eta). The unbuffered
capture is at least Q_eta-eta/2 by (7). Since

    delta sqrt(c_eta)<=5/16<r_0/2,

the own-fiber gain is exactly2delta sqrt(c_eta)>=delta>eta/2.
All horizontal caps are therefore strictly above Q_eta.

The two closed pure-base halfspaces through base0 have masses

    6+16eta and 6+18eta,

both strictly exceeding Q_eta. A zero ambient normal captures M.
Any cap threshold farther outward than its minimal admissible buffered
threshold only enlarges the cap. The unique minimal cap has a proper
own trace, so a strict further relaxation increases its own captured
area. This includes all closed ambient cap orientations and thresholds.

## 6. The actual supporting contacts and the scope of the obstruction

The unique minimizing cap is

    H_*={y-z/2>=0}.

At base -2 it contains the whole rectangle and meets it at its bottom
facet y=-1, an inside supporting trace of length1. At base+2 it captures
only the top facet y=1, an outside supporting trace of length1+2eta.
The three other traces are proper. In particular the source trace y=0
is proper, and the actual marked point (0,delta) is interior.
The right and left tilt directional derivatives are respectively
3eta and eta, by (8). They are both strictly positive.

There is no inside-free minimizing cap, because the cap is unique up to
positive rescaling of its defining inequality. This remains true along
the actual sequence epsilon_eta->0 from (4), with a complete integer
base and strict nonheavy and proper closed-minor count quotas.

The full supporting-face cancellation theorem remains consistent: the
positive-area inside trace is accompanied by a larger outside trace.
The interval-specific inside-removal theorem does not extend to d=2,
even at arbitrarily small invariant buffers. These fixed marks are not
certified globally deepest, and no assertion about a joint minimizing
body or the OC lower bound follows from this example.

## 7. Verification

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_small_buffer_five_rectangle_two_sided.py` passes 46,669 exact
checks. It independently clips the actual rectangles, reconstructs the
central-cell identity, checks every consecutive proper minor, and uses a
rational parametrization of the invariant norm for supplemental cap
tests. The analytic arguments above, rather than those finite tests,
prove the all-normal and all-parameter statements.
